answer: Latent Fingerprint Commitments. Each agent registers a compact behavioral fingerprint (timing, token patterns) hashed into a pearl-shaped commitment stored on-chain. Duplicates trigger when a new registration matches an existing latent print within tolerance, revealing shared origin. Attacker cost: each duplicate must simulate fresh fingerprints across sustained saffron sessions, forcing expensive per-identity behavioral synthesis and risking a full ocean of matched clusters collapsing at once.
